_comment: Price table for LAC-4124 pricing measurement. USD per million tokens.
_verified: 2026-10-16 Anthropic/OpenAI; Gemini rows re-verified 2026-10-27 against the live pricing page (all 3 match; 3.7-flash and 3.5-flash confirmed still unpublished). Fetched from live provider docs, not from a cached model catalog (LAC-3106).

_schema.cache_read: cache hits and refreshes, per MTok
_schema.long_context_threshold: optional; prompt tokens above this switch to the long_* rates
_schema.billing: metered = per-token API billing; subscription = flat-rate seat, no marginal token cost

_notes: Anthropic usage reports input_tokens EXCLUDING cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens, so summing all four categories does not double-count.
OpenAI reports no separate cache-write charge; cache_write is 0 and cached_tokens bill at the cache_read rate.
gpt-5.5 above 272K input tokens moves to a long-context tier not published in the short-context table; long_* rates are intentionally absent so the analyzer fails loudly rather than guessing.
Claude CLI models are billed as a Claude Max/Pro seat, not per token. Marginal cost to Juno is zero; the analyzer reports them separately instead of as $0.00 alongside metered models.

Opus 5.5 computer use requires computer_toolset_20260801, which roughly doubles per-request input overhead (4,530 vs 2,152 tokens, measured 2026-09-22). That overhead is already inside the reported input_tokens; do not add it again.

Keys are BILLING keys, matching what Juno's cost log writes as model_id (cost_log::billing_model_id). Metered API models use the wire model id; subscription paths are prefixed with the provider, so claude-cli:opus is never averaged in with metered Anthropic traffic at $0.00.

Every model in Juno's catalog is keyed here EXCEPT gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.5-flash and gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025, which Google publishes no rate for. They are left out deliberately so this script raises on them rather than scoring them as free; Juno logs those turns at cost_usd 0.0 and warns.

Gemini and OpenAI report prompt tokens INCLUSIVE of cached tokens, unlike Anthropic. Juno subtracts the cached part before writing input_tokens, so the four token fields in a record never double-count on any provider.

Gemini 3.8 Flash is on PROMOTIONAL pricing that ends 2026-12-31: input 0.75 -> 1.50, output 3.75 -> 7.50, cache_read 0.075 -> 0.15 on 2027-01-01, i.e. every rate doubles. The figures here are the promotional ones, verified 2026-10-27. A trial credit or Pro allowance sized on them is wrong from January onward if Gemini 3.8 Flash is in the mix. Re-verify before quoting a price with a lifetime past 2026-12-31.

Google's output price is stated as INCLUDING thinking tokens, which is the pricing-page confirmation of the cost_log rule that output = candidatesTokenCount + thoughtsTokenCount (LAC-5822). candidatesTokenCount alone under-counts a thinking turn.
